newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: GUATEMALA'S PRESIDENT PLEDGES PROBE IN SOCCER TRAGEDY.
newsitem.headline: GUATEMALA'S PRESIDENT PLEDGES PROBE IN SOCCER TRAGEDY.

text.p: Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu on Thursday pledged a full probe into a soccer tragedy in which at least 80 people died and said ticket revenues would be frozen to pay compensation to victims' families.

"The problems cannot and should not be evaded and ignored. We are investigating to be able to say exactly what happened and what were the facts, so that we can learn from this painful experience," Arzu said in a nationwide broadcast that was introduced with a solemn funeral dirge.

In his first public comments since he rushed onto the field with tears in his eyes and declared three days of mourning just after the crush at a World Cup soccer qualifier on Wednesday, Arzu sought to soothe fears of a cover-up of responsibilities.

He announced the formation of a high-level investigative commission, including the interior and health minister, to report back within 15 days to the nation on the causes of the tragedy, in which fans tumbled on top of one another in the overcrowded national soccer stadium, suffocating the victims.
The disaster occurred at a match between Guatemala and Costa Rica and was the worst stadium tragedy in World Cup history.

The cause of the crush is in dispute. The government has said a brawl by unruly fans in the terraces, or bleachers, was the trigger, but officials have also acknowledged there was widespread sale of forged tickets.
Appealing for national unity at a time of deep shock, Arzu responded to calls from victims' families -- many of them among Guatemala's poorest citizens -- for compensation.
"I have asked the comptroller general to take charge of the funds collected at the (soccer) event so that they can be used to indemnify the families of the dead victims," he said.
He also promised an "extensive audit" of the top national sporting confederation stretching back at least two years.
